papers.relied_on: V14 row 14 D7 used 86.3 million US adults with MASLD in 2020 as the base of the patient-count chain.
papers.full_text_shows: The 86.3 million (33.7 percent of US adults) and 14.9 million MASH figures are model outputs of an agent-based microsimulation calibrated to NHANES 2017-2018, not survey counts. The text gives no share with type 2 diabetes (only 'more than 60% ... having diabetes, obesity, or both') and no share evaluated per year, so the 75 percent and 5 percent shares in V14 stay assumptions.
papers.quote: the model estimated that 33.7% of the US adult population, or 86.3 million people, had MASLD in 2020.
papers.key_numbers: MASLD 86.3 million (2020), 101.2 million (2030), 121.9 million (2050); MASH 14.9 million (2020); MASH with fibrosis F2 or higher 6.7 million (2020); 11,483 new HCC and 1,717 liver transplants per year 2020-2025; simulated 2,821,624 agents.
papers.role_in_work: Epidemiological base for the D7 chain of row 14 (and the broader note for row 19 text in corpus.csv).
papers.design: Decision-analytic agent-based state-transition model (microsimulation), yearly cycle, STRESS reporting; Cleveland Clinic.
papers.population_and_size: US adults, model population of 2,821,624 simulated individuals; outputs scaled to the US population.
papers.measure_type: None (no insulin, C-peptide or insulin-resistance measure in the paper); disease-burden model only.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not applicable; NHANES 2017-2018 used for calibration.
papers.quality_note: Model with stated assumptions (incidence rising to 2030); validated against NHANES, SEER and UNOS. Peer-reviewed, no measurement content. The MASLD definition counts steatosis with cardiometabolic risk, not the guideline population 'suspected MASLD without T2D'.

papers.relied_on: No score entry cites it; listed in corpus.csv as V16 text only (search record).
papers.full_text_shows: One 71-year-old man with a large unresectable pelvic sarcoma and glucose below 40 mg/dL had low insulin and C-peptide with low IGF-1; IGF-2 could not be measured. NICTH was diagnosed from hypoinsulinemic hypoglycemia, low C-peptide and tumour burden after excluding other causes; the paper then cites an IGF-2/IGF-1 molar ratio above 10 as indicative (secondhand, its ref 2).
papers.quote: It can be confirmed through the presence of hypoinsulinemic hypoglycemia alongside low C-peptide levels in patients with significant tumor burden
papers.key_numbers: Glucose 40 mg/dL; insulin 0.4 (table unit printed as ug/ml, reference 2.6-24.9, so the unit is probably a typo for uIU/mL); C-peptide 0.6 ng/mL (reference 1.1-4.4); IGF-1 25.6 ng/mL (38.3-182.5); glucose requirement 600 g/day; one patient.
papers.role_in_work: Additional case report for row 21 (NICTH): insulin and C-peptide suppressed during hypoglycaemia to point away from insulinoma; also a secondary text citation for the IGF-2/IGF-1 ratio above 10 that row 21 marks [recall].
papers.population_and_size: n = 1, male, 71 years, pelvic pleomorphic sarcoma, Iran.
papers.measure_type: Random (spot) insulin and C-peptide drawn during hypoglycaemia; not post-meal, post-load or stimulated.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not stated; IGF-2 not available in the country.
papers.quality_note: Case report, no comparator, IGF-2 confirmation missing; insulin unit inconsistent in the table. Supports the sequence only at case level.

papers.relied_on: V15 row 14 D8 listed it among four records that gave no increment of HOMA-IR over FIB-4 (abstract level).
papers.full_text_shows: In 322 Dutch children (8-18 years) with obesity or overweight plus a risk factor, ALT was the screening test; HOMA-IR entered the logistic model only as one covariate (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00-1.13 per unit, P = .039 in the table) and was not one of the noninvasive scores compared by AUROC. No test beat ALT, so the paper contains no HOMA-IR versus FIB-4 comparison.
papers.quote: No test performed significantly better than ALT
papers.key_numbers: n = 322; VCTE 7.4 kPa or more in 1.9% (normal ALT), 16.4%, 21.3%, 38.9% (ALT 80 IU/L or more); ALT at sex-specific ULN sensitivity 98% (95% CI 95-100), specificity 20% (15-25); ALT 29 IU/L sensitivity 95%, specificity 39% (33-45); HOMA-IR OR 1.10 (1.00-1.13).
papers.role_in_work: Evidence for row 14 D8 that no incremental value of HOMA-IR over simpler tests was found; paediatric, so only indirectly relevant to the adult guideline population.
papers.design: Prospective population-based screening cohort with transient elastography (VCTE) as reference; no biopsy.
papers.population_and_size: 322 children aged 8-18 with obesity, or overweight plus one additional MASLD risk factor; Netherlands, 64% male, median age 13.
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (fasting insulin and glucose giving HOMA-IR) as one covariate; ALT is the screening test.
papers.assay_or_platform: Routine hospital laboratory; VCTE (FibroScan) with CAP; HOMA-IR assay not specified in the text read.
papers.quality_note: PDF text extraction (two columns) is partly interleaved and the table values for HOMA-IR are lost, so only the abstract and discussion numbers were used. Reference standard is elastography, not histology. Paediatric population.

papers.relied_on: V1 row 49 D7 used it for 'modelled about 350,000 stage 1 and 140,000 stage 2 in US children and adults'.
papers.full_text_shows: The 350,000 figure is the number of US children expected to be multiple-autoantibody positive (stage 1 and 2 together) when extrapolating the Colorado ASK programme. Table 4 lists stage 1 prevalent persons as 280,000 children and 400,000 adults, stage 2 as 70,000 and 70,000 (140,000 total), and stage 3 new patients as 25,000 children and 35,000 adults per year. The numbers are prevalence extrapolations, not counts of identified people.
papers.quote: would be found to express multiple islet autoantibodies
papers.key_numbers: Table 4 (USA): stage 1 prevalent 280,000 children + 400,000 adults; stage 2 prevalent 70,000 + 70,000; stage 3 new per year 25,000 + 35,000; 700,000 children with any islet autoantibody if all 70 million aged 1-17 were screened, half (350,000) multiple; about 11,000 of 3.59 million US births per year progress to type 1 diabetes by age 15.
papers.role_in_work: Source of the prevalent pool of stage 1 and 2 type 1 diabetes in the US used as a note for the row 49 D7 count (not counted in the score).
papers.design: Narrative review of health-economic analyses with modelled prevalence extrapolation (Table 4).
papers.population_and_size: US children and adults; extrapolation from ASK (Colorado), TEDDY and Fr1da (Germany, more than 90,000 children).
papers.measure_type: Islet autoantibody screening with glucose staging (A1c, OGTT); no insulin or C-peptide measure is evaluated.
papers.assay_or_platform: Autoantibodies to insulin, GAD, IA-2, ZnT8; OGTT glucose staging (Table 1).
papers.quality_note: Single-author review, declares no conflicts of interest. Prevalence figures are extrapolations with unstated ranges. No insulin or C-peptide content, so it cannot support a C-peptide or OGTT-insulin use.

papers.relied_on: No score entry cites it; listed in corpus.csv as V16 text only (search record).
papers.full_text_shows: In 14 patients with type B insulin resistance (before and after remission) and 14 matched patients with lipodystrophy, NMR lipoprotein profiles did not follow the degree of insulin resistance: active type B disease (HOMA-IR median 451.9) had a less atherogenic profile than remission (HOMA-IR 3.1) and lipodystrophy. It is a mechanistic study with no clinical decision, test threshold or outcome.
papers.quote: pro-atherogenic alterations in lipids are not driven by resistance to insulin action
papers.key_numbers: TBIR n = 14 (median 1.1 years between visits); HOMA-IR 451.9 [182.6, 816.2] active vs 3.1 [1.6, 7.8] remission (P = 0.0002); lipodystrophy HOMA-IR 11.9 [8.9, 43.3]; active TBIR defined by fasting insulin above 100 mcU/mL plus receptor antibodies.
papers.role_in_work: Mechanistic background only; at most context for row 12 (severe or syndromic IR) and for the point that HOMA-IR/insulin-based IR measures do not track lipid risk in selective IR. No claim in the verified files depends on it.
papers.design: Cross-sectional and paired before/after observational study with NMR lipoprotein profiling.
papers.population_and_size: 14 patients with type B IR (NIH cohort) and 14 matched patients with lipodystrophy.
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR) as descriptors; NMR lipoprotein particles are the outcome.
papers.assay_or_platform: NIH Clinical Center laboratory insulin; Vantera 400-MHz NMR analyzer (LipoScience); Roche Cobas 6000.
papers.quality_note: Small rare-disease cohorts, no hard cardiovascular endpoints (stated by the authors). Not a diagnostic or decision study.

papers.relied_on: V15 row 46 D2 listed it among small case reports behind the Japanese C-peptide criterion (abstract level).
papers.full_text_shows: A 10-month-old Japanese girl with ketoacidosis, HbA1c not markedly raised and a glucagon-stimulation test: C-peptide below 0.6 ng/mL at baseline and unchanged after glucagon. She met the Japanese criteria; GAD and IA-2 antibodies were negative, insulin autoantibody positive. The paper adds HLA and CSAD genotype findings; no accuracy data and no cutoff analysis.
papers.quote: with markedly low C-peptide and relatively low HbA1c levels
papers.key_numbers: C-peptide below 0.6 ng/mL at baseline and after glucagon; n = 1; HLA DRB1*04:05-DQB1*04:01 present; CSAD rs3782151 homozygous risk allele; later Graves disease at 8 years 8 months.
papers.role_in_work: Case-level support for row 46 (fulminant type 1 diabetes, C-peptide criterion); shows glucagon-stimulated C-peptide used in practice in an infant.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, fasting (baseline) and glucagon-stimulated, at onset.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not stated in the text read; the reported detection limit appears to be 0.6 ng/mL, which is above the 0.3 ng/mL fasting cutoff of the Japanese criteria quoted in row 46.
papers.quality_note: Case report. Because the reported value is '< 0.6' it cannot show that the stricter cutoffs in the criteria were met; the paper states the criteria were fulfilled.

papers.relied_on: U1 row 13 D3 and V20 row 45 D3 scored 2 because the ADA 2026 recommendations name a drug and a condition but not an insulin or HOMA measurement.
papers.full_text_shows: Recommendation 3.13 conditions pioglitazone on 'evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes' without naming a test; only the supporting text describes IRIS entry as HOMA-IR 3.0 or more in people with a stroke or TIA in the previous 6 months. Recommendation 3.7 (metformin, including prior gestational diabetes) and the rest of section 3 mention no insulin, C-peptide or HOMA measure for gestational diabetes.
papers.quote: In people with a history of stroke and evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes, pioglitazone may be considered
papers.key_numbers: Rec 3.13 'may be considered'; IRIS: HOMA-IR 3.0 or more, recent (under 6 months) stroke or TIA, 4.8 years follow-up, pioglitazone goal dose 45 mg; Rec 3.7 metformin 'should be considered' in high-risk adults and prior GDM.
papers.role_in_work: US guideline text for the D3 scores of rows 13 and 45 (and the GL-12 claim that no guideline requires an insulin-resistance measurement).
papers.population_and_size: Adults at risk of or with prediabetes; recommendation 3.13 for people with prior stroke or TIA and evidence of insulin resistance.
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (HOMA-IR) only in the trial description in the text; none recommended.
papers.quality_note: Local copy is a PMC page text and appears complete for the recommendations read. A quirk: the grade letters in the page text are interleaved, so the evidence grade of 3.13 was not read from this copy.

proposals.reason: The 86.3 million base is confirmed, but it is a modelled figure for all MASLD; the T2D share and the yearly evaluated share remain assumptions, so the paper alone does not move the bin. Alternative bin 4 is already named in V14.
proposals.quote: the model estimated that 33.7% of the US adult population, or 86.3 million people, had MASLD in 2020.

proposals.reason: C307 contains no HOMA-IR versus FIB-4 comparison (HOMA-IR is only a regression covariate with OR 1.10) in children; this agrees with 'no incremental-value analysis found' and does not support 0 or 2.
proposals.quote: No test performed significantly better than ALT

proposals.reason: Score counts identified patients, not prevalent undetected stage 1 and 2; the paper's Table 4 (prevalence extrapolations) is correctly excluded. Only the wording of the prevalence figure in the V1 reason needs correcting.
proposals.quote: would be found to express multiple islet autoantibodies

proposals.reason: A single case report with glucagon-stimulated C-peptide below 0.6 ng/mL is case-series level evidence; no accuracy data, so 1 stands.

The phrase 'evidence of insulin resistance' in the recommendation itself is the only link to measurement, and the HOMA-IR 3.0 appears in supporting text only.

Rec 3.7 and section 3 name metformin and prior GDM but no insulin or HOMA measure; text confirms the measurement is not addressed, so 1 is arguably the literal anchor, but clarification 5 and the V20 choice stand. claim_issues.where: usecases/scoring/V1.json row 49 D7 reason (and any copy in the ranking text)
claim_issues.issue: States 'modelled about 350,000 stage 1 and 140,000 stage 2 in US children and adults'. In PMID 40555704 the 350,000 is the number of US children expected to be multiple-autoantibody positive (stage 1 and 2 together); Table 4 gives stage 1 prevalent persons as 280,000 children plus 400,000 adults and stage 2 as 70,000 plus 70,000. The figures are extrapolations, not counts of identified people. The score is unaffected because prevalent unidentified persons are not counted.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Modelled US prevalence (Table 4): stage 1 about 280,000 children and 400,000 adults; stage 2 about 70,000 children and 70,000 adults; extrapolated from Colorado ASK data, not counts of identified people.

claim_issues.issue: C303 states the ratio rule, but only secondhand (its reference 2) and the case itself had no IGF-2 measurement, so it can be cited as a secondary source, not as confirmation. It is also a further case report where suppressed insulin and C-peptide steered the diagnosis.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Case report PMID 40045285 (DOI 10.1186/s12902-025-01885-5, full text) cites an IGF-2/IGF-1 molar ratio above 10 as indicative of NICTH (secondhand); in its own patient IGF-2 was not measured and the diagnosis rested on hypoinsulinemic hypoglycemia with low C-peptide and IGF-1 and a large tumour.

claim_issues.where: usecases/scoring/V14.json row 14 D7 reason: 'MASLD 86.3 million US adults in 2020 (model, PMID 39821400)'
claim_issues.issue: Accurate, but the chain's 75 percent without T2D has no support in the paper (it says only that more than 60 percent of patients with MASLD have diabetes, obesity or both), so the share stays an assumption.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: MASLD 86.3 million US adults in 2020 (model output, PMID 39821400); the paper gives no share with type 2 diabetes.
